body: Could all of this not be compacted to a `vec3[16]` and assigned to with a loop? I'd expect performance to be unaffected, so the more compact code might be worth it.
Same as the texture reads, can this not be tidied up by putting everything into a loop?
I don't really understand what's going on here :|
Seems unused.
The depth is multiplied by a lot to make sure it's fully opaque, instead of having things further away turn transparent
It's a leftover of previous work, I'm currently keeping it around for various experiments

I just found this easier to implement, I've had plenty of issues in the past with for loops not compiling and I'm kinda coding blind as I just get a result in the form of it compiles or not, and if not I get no errors beyond "oh shader is null" which is Highly useless feedback.
Same as texture reads
I suspect there's very little to gain from that given 80% of the cost of TAA is the imagestore at the end, and such micro optimizations can be done later.

> I get no errors beyond "oh shader is null"

If I intentionally add an error to the shader, I do get actual error logs.

What I do is I pipe the Godot output to a log file, so something like this: `$GODOT &> log.txt`, and then open the log file with a code/text editor.

The shader errors are at the start of the log, because that's when they get compiled. Without redirecting to a log file they just get buried by the error spam, but they're still there.
Seems weird to me that one `imageStore` would be 80% of the cost when the shader is already performing several texture reads and a bunch of math. How/where did you get this 80% metric?

I thought I already submitted this comment in the review but seems like I forgot. Oh well, anyway.

From https://www.elopezr.com/temporal-aa-and-the-quest-for-the-holy-trail/

> Jorge Jiménez further optimized it by discarding the corner samples down to 5 reads for [Call of Duty](https://research.activision.com/publications/archives/filmic-smaasharp-morphological-and-temporal-antialiasing).

Apparently, it's possible to further reduce the amount of texture reads from 9 to 5 by ignoring the corners, though at the cost of some quality loss.

Not saying this should be implemented, just wanted to point out that this is an option.

I removed EVERYTHING except that, and measured TAA's cost before and after. I don't quite get it why it's so expensive either, and it's rather frustrating, as if it weren't, TAA costs would be actually around what I'd expect TAA to cost, instead of triple that.

Idk, when working with TAA resolve shader and that shader specifically I just get the spam of null shader, with absolutely no trace of an error as to why it's failed to compile. Other shaders I played around with inside of Godot I do remember getting proper error messages.

I cannot reproduce, or at least not to this extent. On my machine, through the visual profiler, I get these timings:
- normal: ~1.55ms
- `imageStore` only, no compute: ~0.51ms
- no `imageStore`, no compute: ~0.43ms

So while running with `imageStore` only seems to have a cost, it's possible the bulk of that cost comes from just launching the compute shader.

For me the cost is ~0.8ms normal, and without compute ~0.6ms tho I have not tried no compute and no imagestore.
I am on an RX 6600, running at 1440p
RX570 at 1080p here.
